findings.requirement: An isolated child failure must never produce an empty-success coverage result.
findings.finding: The close handler accepts any syntactically valid { errors: string[] } document before checking the child exit code or signal. A child that writes {"errors":[]} and then exits nonzero or is signaled is therefore returned as { errors: [] }. The comment says a zero exit means protocol completion, but the implementation does not enforce that invariant.
findings.requiredRepair: Accept the parsed report only when code === 0 and signal is null. For every nonzero exit or signal, return a nonempty isolated-composition failure even if stdout contains a valid empty report. Add a deterministic child-protocol test that writes a valid empty report and exits nonzero, plus a signaled/aborted equivalent if the harness exposes it.
findings.resolution: Resolved: parsed child output is accepted only when exit code is zero and signal is null; every other close state returns a nonempty isolated-composition failure.
